stem.text: Which set of steps is the best method for conducting the emulsion test for lipids?

A.text: Add $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of water to the sample.
Pour the water into a test-tube containing $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of ethanol.
Lipids are present if the mixture becomes cloudy.

B.text: Add $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of ethanol to the sample and shake.
Pour the ethanol into a test-tube containing $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of water and boil.
Lipids are present if the mixture becomes clear.

C.text: Add $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of water to the sample and shake.
Pour the water into a test-tube containing $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of ethanol and boil.
Lipids are present if the mixture becomes cloudy.

D.text: Add $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of ethanol to the sample and shake.
Pour the ethanol into a test-tube containing $2\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of water and shake again.
Lipids are present if the mixture becomes cloudy.
